summary: Iteration 22: Comprehensive testing of Cross-Border Watch module (Bangladesh & Myanmar intelligence engine). All 17 backend API tests passed (100%). All frontend UI components verified working correctly. The Cross-Border Watch page renders with two country sections, watchpoints card, signal filters, expandable items with 'What happened', 'India-relevant implication', and 'Early warning' sections.
passed_tests: GET /api/cross-border/watch returns 200
Response contains bangladesh section with items, count, posture
Response contains myanmar section with items, count, posture
Response contains watchpoints array
Response contains signal_distribution object
Posture values are valid (stable/watchful/elevated/deteriorating)
Items have required fields: id, title, severity, priority_score
Items have optional signal fields (signal_strength, signal_bucket, india_relevance_score) - currently empty for pre-update items
GET /api/cross-border/watch?min_signal=HIGH returns 200
GET /api/cross-border/watch?min_signal=MEDIUM returns 200
HIGH filter only returns HIGH signal items
MEDIUM filter returns HIGH + MEDIUM signal items
Items have geo_boost and effective_priority fields
Items sorted by effective_priority descending
GET /api/intelligence still works
GET /api/feedback/stats still works
GET /api/training/effectiveness still works
Frontend: Cross-Border Watch page renders with title 'CROSS-BORDER WATCH'
Frontend: Bangladesh Intelligence section visible with item count (50) and STABLE posture badge
Frontend: Myanmar Intelligence section visible with item count (23) and ELEVATED posture badge
Frontend: Watchpoints card shows detected trends (5 watchpoints)
Frontend: Signal filter buttons (ALL/MEDIUM/HIGH) visible and functional
Frontend: Clicking signal item expands to show 'What happened', 'India-relevant implication', 'Early warning'
Frontend: Each item shows priority score, severity badge, signal strength badge
Frontend: Filter behavior correct - ALL(73) >= MEDIUM(52) >= HIGH(52)
critical_code_review_comments: Cross-border endpoint correctly splits items by Bangladesh/Myanmar using countries_involved, regions, state fields
_compute_posture uses avg_priority + escalation_ratio to determine posture (deteriorating/elevated/watchful/stable)
_compute_watchpoints extracts top 5 themes from signal_bucket and early_warning_signal
_apply_geo_boost adds +2-3 to effective_priority for items mentioning border locations (Moreh, Champhai, Cox's Bazar, etc.)
Signal filtering correctly uses MongoDB query: signal_strength='HIGH' or signal_strength in ['HIGH','MEDIUM']
Items without signal_strength/signal_bucket are expected - processed before AI prompt update
Frontend SignalItem component correctly handles expand/collapse with 'What happened', 'India-relevant implication', 'Early warning' sections
Frontend CountrySection component correctly displays posture badges with appropriate colors (red=deteriorating, orange=elevated, amber=watchful, emerald=stable)
test_credentials: No credentials needed - app has no auth system
seed_data_creation: None - used existing cross-border items in database
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 22 tested the Cross-Border Watch module. GET /api/cross-border/watch returns bangladesh and myanmar sections with items, count, posture. Signal filtering works via min_signal query param (HIGH/MEDIUM). Most items don't have signal_bucket/signal_strength/india_relevance_score yet because they were processed before the AI prompt was updated - new items will have these fields. Current data: 50 Bangladesh items, 23 Myanmar items. Watchpoints are extracted from signal_bucket and early_warning_signal fields. Geographic boost adds +2-3 to effective_priority for border locations. Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_cross_border_watch_v22.py
